title: Coal conveyor, head pulley lagging worn
tests: Thin notes; natural deterioration; does the AI ask the right questions instead of inventing?
summary: Coal conveyor CV-12 tripped on belt slip three times in a week. The fitter's notes are short. Lagging on the head pulley looked worn smooth. Only two evidence items, one tree node beyond the event. Tests that the AI points at gaps and does not invent facts.

problem.title: Belt slip trips on coal conveyor CV-12
problem.site: Coal handling plant, Bowen Basin QLD
problem.whatHappened: CV-12 tripped three times on belt-slip protection over one week. Head pulley lagging looked worn smooth when inspected.
problem.impact: Coal delivery stops on each trip.
problem.duty: Raw coal to the coal handling plant, 900 t/h

evidence.title: Head pulley lagging
evidence.note: Ceramic diamond pattern worn smooth across the middle third of the pulley face.

evidence.title: Belt slip trip log
evidence.note: 3 trips on belt slip: 1, 3 and 4 Sep. No time of day recorded.

problemDraft.roughNotes: cv12 head pulley lagging smooth. belt slip trip x3 this week mostly when its wet. fitter re-set the tension on thursday. need to relag.

draft.notes: cv12 head pulley lagging smooth. belt slip trip x3 this week mostly when its wet. fitter re-set the tension on thursday. need to relag.

mustSuggest.idea: Wet coal or water on the belt face reducing grip, with a way to check (belt cleaning, scrapers, rain protection)
Belt tension low or take-up not working, because the fitter re-set it
No lagging wear measurement in inspection route or PM plan
Lagging wear not measured on rounds because there is no limit to measure against

acceptable: Carry-back or build-up on the pulley
Belt cover wear or speed mismatch
Lagging type unsuitable for wet duty
wrongOrDangerous: Anything stating the lagging wore out in a specific number of hours

mustFlag.note: Only a physical cause is listed
No human or system cause anywhere
Wear with natural or forced not decided

mustNotFlag: stating the lagging is the proven root
challenge.expectation: Summary says the analysis is just started; asks what changed in the weather, belt condition and tension history.
deliberateWeaknesses: Notes and tree very thin: no cause beyond the lagging
n1 is a flagged root that is still only a hypothesis, with action a1 against it
Wet weather and tension re-set not explored

capa.deteriorationReasoning: Lagging smooth at the pulley centre may be normal wear or wear we caused (wet coal, carry-back, low tension). Check lagging age and hours run, scraper condition and tension record to decide.
corrective: Re-lag the head pulley (a1): the AI may restate it only if not repeating a1

preventive.what: Lagging thickness and pattern check against a minimum, with photo
Lagging or a lagged spare pulley held, if the lagging life is found to be natural wear
Record the take-up tension or position on the job plan after any re-set

capa.spares: Lagging material or a spare lagged head pulley, to be sized after the lagging life is known; do not give a part number or price.
capa.rollout: Other coal conveyors with ceramic lagging and wet-weather exposure.
unacceptable: Declaring natural or forced with confidence
Inventing a lagging life in hours

mustInclude: CV-12 tripped on belt-slip protection three times in a week
mustNotInvent: the date of the Thursday reset
gapsToPointOut: What dates and times were the trips, and what was the weather?
How long since the head pulley was last lagged?
What was the tension before and after the reset?
Are there scrapers or belt cleaners and what is their condition?

mustInclude: Report is short and says the data is thin
stillToConfirm: owner and date not set on a1

hardChecks.allowedNumbersNote: Numbers in the AI output must come from this list or from the app's own cost calculation (buildAiContext loss line). Anything else is invented.
wordingRules: No N#, A# or E# labels inside prose
No dates as YYYY-MM-DD in prose
